## BUILDER CONTEXT
# Builder Profile — Sam

## Role
Solo founder and full-stack engineer. Building across multiple projects simultaneously.
Primary consumer of all generated specs — implementation guides must be self-contained.

## Active Projects (2026)
- **sam-plugin** — personal OpenClaw plugin (this project); wires agent to Sam's live systems
- **spec-doc** — this tool (Flask :3101 + Angular :4201); documentation-first dev methodology
- **humanize-me** — live Flask + Next.js AI humanizer; production at humaniz.me
- **Bubls** — Ionic + Capacitor mobile app (event discovery, Zürich); Angular + Flask
- **Trendfy** — wardrobai/trendfy.me; AI fashion photoshoot; kill date passed, status TBD
- **OpenClaw** — local AI agent gateway; runs claude-cli provider, Telegram-connected

## Stack Preferences
- **Backend**: Python / Flask (thin, ~150 lines, Blueprints, openapi.yaml-first)
- **Frontend (web)**: Angular (standalone components, signals) or Next.js 15 + shadcn/ui
- **Frontend (mobile)**: Ionic + Capacitor (iOS 16+, Angular)
- **AI**: Claude CLI (dev) → Anthropic SDK (prod); chain adapter pattern
- **Deploy**: Docker Compose → Coolify; single gunicorn + nginx pattern
- **Agent platform**: OpenClaw (local gateway, claude-cli provider, Telegram channel)

## Engineering Preferences
- Brain dump → AI structures it → ship. Minimal viable shape, not maximum abstraction
- Small focused modules with clear boundaries — no god classes, no god files
- Adapter pattern for all external services (AI, DB, storage)
- In-process state (module-level dict + threading.Lock) is fine for single-consumer async
- No speculative abstractions — build for the one concrete case that exists now
- Files under 200 lines; named exports; one component per file
- Build order: frontend with mock data first → Flask built to match the UI's API contract

## Known Constraints
- Solo developer — no handoff; guides must be runnable by one person end-to-end
- No Redis, no Postgres (unless Supabase via Flask), no external queue
- Claude CLI subprocess timeout: 3600s; Anthropic SDK: no practical ceiling
- OpenClaw workspace plugin system: skills first (SKILL.md files), graduate to full plugin when needed
- Telegram is the primary mobile interface — responses must stay under 4096 chars


## ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES (non-negotiable — follow these patterns)
# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

## P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles
- Skills first: start with `SKILL.md` files (no build step, iterate fast)
- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)

## P7 — File Size & Structure
- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

## Code Rules
- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context
- `read_context()` returns `""` for missing files; `PromptBuilder.section()` skips empty content


## CONTEXT FROM EPIC (generated in prior step)
# 🎯 Epic: thin-api-phase3

## Business Value

The frontend currently knows too much. `ai.service.ts` ships hardcoded Claude prompt instructions in TypeScript — nine distinct text actions all funnel through `/api/ai/text/rewrite` with instruction blobs assembled client-side. Every prompt tweak forces an Angular rebuild and deploy, and the boundary between "UI behavior" and "AI behavior" is smeared across both layers. For a solo founder iterating on prompt quality, that round-trip cost is paid weekly.

Phase 3 finishes the thin-API migration started in Phase 2 by exposing eight flat, action-named routes under `/api/text/*`. Each route is a ~10-line Python handler that delegates to a SKILL.md file — the single source of truth for what Claude is told. The frontend collapses to data-in / result-out: `{ text }` → `{ text, latencyMs }`. Prompts become a backend artifact, deployable independently, ownable by the agent layer rather than the UI layer.

The payoff is compounding: future text actions ship as one SKILL.md + one ten-line route, no frontend deploy. Dead code (`text_prompts.py` at 423 LOC, three uncalled routes, the entire TypeScript instruction-string tree) leaves the repo. The codebase gets smaller and the iteration loop on AI behavior gets shorter — the only two metrics that matter for a one-person product team.

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers
- **Eight flat text routes** under `/api/text/*` — `brainstorm`, `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`, `rewrite` — each a thin Flask handler delegating to a skill
- **SKILL.md authorship** for any of the eight actions that don't already have one (existing: `brainstorm`, `rewrite`; the other six need inventory + creation)
- **Frontend cutover** — `ai.service.ts` rewritten with `/api/text` base, named methods, zero instruction strings
- **Followup brainstorm pattern** resolved into the new contract (single endpoint with optional fields, decided in architecture)
- **`style` enum contract** for `/rewrite` — `Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy` — validated at the route boundary
- **Dead code deletion** after cutover: legacy `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate`, `/api/ai/text/iterate`, `/api/ai/text/lint-braindump`, `/api/ai/text/review` routes; `text_prompts.py` and its tests; instruction strings and the `generate()` method in `ai.service.ts`

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover
- ❌ **`bootstrap-project` migration** — async multi-step chain stays on `/api/ai/text/bootstrap-project`; explicitly Phase 4
- ❌ **`generate-epic-guide` migration** — stays on `/api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide`; explicitly Phase 4
- ❌ **Generic `/api/text/generate` replacement** — the old `/generate` endpoint is deleted with no successor
- ❌ **`quality/` module audit** — separate audit work, not blocking Phase 3
- ❌ **`task_gen.py` audit** — separate audit work, not blocking Phase 3
- ❌ **New text actions beyond the eight** — re-scope only if a concrete caller appears
- ❌ **Project CRUD or file-save endpoint changes** — `/api/projects/*` routes untouched

## Tasks

| # | Task | Dependencies | Parallel | Effort | Priority |
|---|------|--------------|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | **Inventory & author SKILL.md files** | None | — | 1 day | High |
| 2 | **Build `/api/text/*` Flask blueprint (8 routes)** | Task 1 | — | 1 day | High |
| 3 | **Cut `ai.service.ts` over to `/api/text` + resolve followup-brainstorm caller** | Task 2 | — | 1 day | High |
| 4 | **Delete dead routes, `text_prompts.py`, and frontend instruction strings** | Task 3 | — | 0.5 days | High |
| 5 | **End-to-end smoke test of all 8 actions** | Task 3 | Task 4 | 0.5 days | Low |

## Success Criteria

- ✅ All 8 actions reachable at `POST /api/text/<action>` and return `{ text, latencyMs }`
- ✅ `/api/text/rewrite` is the only route accepting a second body field (`style`); the other 7 accept `{ text }` only
- ✅ Invalid `style` values for `/rewrite` are rejected at the route boundary with a 4xx response
- ✅ `ai.service.ts` contains zero instruction/prompt strings — no hardcoded "You are a..." text anywhere in the frontend
- ✅ `ai.service.ts` base path is `/api/text`; the string `/api/ai/text` no longer appears outside bootstrap/epic-guide callers
- ✅ `text_prompts.py` is deleted and no module in the repo imports it
- ✅ Legacy routes `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/generate`, `/iterate`, `/lint-braindump`, `/review` return 404
- ✅ `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` endpoints continue to function unchanged
- ✅ `app.component.ts` followup-brainstorm flow works through the new contract with no inline instruction strings
- ✅ Each new Python route file stays under 200 lines; each handler is ~10 lines

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving this epic
- [Solution Architecture](./architecture.md) – System design
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking

Design the solution architecture to fulfill the tasks and scope defined above.

- `CHAIN_PROVIDER=cli` → subprocess `claude -p` (local dev + Docker)

## REFERENCE CODE (port from, not code in the target repo)
# Reference Code — Patterns to Port

These are real working patterns from sibling projects. When architecture says "port from references.md",
describe the shape to port — not the implementation detail.

## financing-plugin — Claude Code Plugin Structure

The gold standard for a well-structured Claude Code plugin.
Location: `~/Projects/financing-plugin-extracted/`

### Plugin Layout Pattern
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # Plugin metadata + version
├── agents/                      # Specialised agents as flat .md files
├── hooks/                       # SessionStart hook (context injection)
├── references/                  # Convention references (single source of truth)
├── skills/                      # Skills — each a SKILL.md
│   ├── SKILL_MAP.md             # Master index of all skills
│   ├── feature-pipeline/SKILL.md   # Orchestrator skill
│   ├── feature-requirement/SKILL.md
│   └── dev-build/SKILL.md       # Dev tools
└── docs/                        # Spec-doc specs (Epic, Architecture)
```

Key rule: **references are the source of truth** — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills.
Skills read from `references/*.md`, never inline the same constraint twice.

### SessionStart Hook Pattern
The hook fires on every session start and injects live context into the agent.
No heavy I/O — just read files and compute a snapshot. Fast and deterministic.

### Skill File Pattern (SKILL.md)
```markdown
# Skill Name

## When to use
[Trigger conditions]

## What I do
[Steps the agent takes]

## Tools available
[Bash, Read, Write, etc.]

## Examples
[Sample invocations]
```

## OpenClaw Workspace Files — Context Injection Pattern

The workspace files already loaded by OpenClaw every session:
- `AGENTS.md` — session instructions (auto-loaded)
- `USER.md` — who Sam is (auto-loaded)
- `MEMORY.md` — curated long-term memory (auto-loaded in main session)
- `TOOLS.md` — stack + environment (auto-loaded)

Port pattern: new skills should reference these files rather than duplicating their content.
`SOUL.md` defines agent identity — skills can refer to it for tone/style.

## spec-doc Bootstrap Adapter — Async 202 + Polling Pattern

Already shipping in spec-doc. Port this pattern for any long-running skill:
1. POST trigger → return 202 + job_id immediately
2. Background thread runs the work
3. GET /status/{job_id} polls until `done: true`
4. In-process dict keyed by project/job id — no Redis needed

Location: `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/text.py` (bootstrap)
and `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/task_gen.py` (generate-task)

## Trendfy — Docker + Deploy Pattern

gunicorn config for Flask with background threads:
```
gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:3101 --workers 1 --threads 4 --timeout 900 --worker-class gthread
```
`--workers 1` required when using in-process state dicts (no cross-worker sharing).
`gthread` allows daemon threads to coexist with gunicorn.

## humanize-me — Flask Thin Layer Pattern

Flask as a ~150 line AI service boundary:
- All routes: validate → call AI adapter → return streaming or JSON
- No business logic in routes
- Supabase accessed only through Flask, never from frontend directly


## CONTENT ROUTING RULES (violations are failures)
- Status words (Done, In Progress, Completed) → ONLY in timeline.md
- Code blocks with implementation → ONLY in implementation guides
- Business value and market analysis → ONLY in epic.md
- Design decisions and tech stack → ONLY in architecture.md
- Step-by-step instructions → ONLY in implementation guides
- Problem identification → ONLY in analysis.md
- Cross-references MUST be bidirectional (if A→B then B→A)
- Always use "Solution Architecture" (not just "Architecture") in cross-references
## Your ONE Job
System design, decisions, trade-offs. NO code blocks. NO status.

## Output Format
OUTPUT ONLY markdown. Start with #. No preamble.

# Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Dead routes and dead Python deleted

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/text/brainstorm   { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/expand       { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/compress     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/clarify      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/simplify     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/tldr         { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/bullets      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/rewrite      { text, style }       → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (unchanged for Phase 3)

Bootstrap-project is a complex multi-step async Python workflow. Not a Phase 3 concern. Leave the existing endpoints.

```
POST   /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project
GET    /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/text/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes are gone)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- All instruction strings in `ai.service.ts` (the brainstorm prompt array, the style instruction map, etc.)
- The `generate()` method
- The `base = '/api/ai/text'` string

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end
5. Delete old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` routes
6. Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests
7. Delete dead TypeScript

Focus on WHY. Explain trade-offs. No code blocks.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)

- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

## Code Rules
- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context

# 🎯 Epic: thin-api-phase3

## Business Value

The frontend currently knows too much. `ai.service.ts` ships hardcoded Claude prompt instructions in TypeScript — nine distinct text actions all funnel through `/api/ai/text/rewrite` with instruction blobs assembled client-side. Every prompt tweak forces an Angular rebuild and deploy, and the boundary between "UI behavior" and "AI behavior" is smeared across both layers. For a solo founder iterating on prompt quality, that round-trip cost is paid weekly.

Phase 3 finishes the thin-API migration started in Phase 2 by exposing eight flat, action-named routes under `/api/text/*`. Each route is a ~10-line Python handler that delegates to a SKILL.md file — the single source of truth for what Claude is told. The frontend collapses to data-in / result-out: `{ text }` → `{ text, latencyMs }`. Prompts become a backend artifact, deployable independently, ownable by the agent layer rather than the UI layer.

The payoff is compounding: future text actions ship as one SKILL.md + one ten-line route, no frontend deploy. Dead code (`text_prompts.py` at 423 LOC, three uncalled routes, the entire TypeScript instruction-string tree) leaves the repo. # Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Dead routes and dead Python deleted

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/text/brainstorm   { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/expand       { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/compress     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/clarify      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/simplify     { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/tldr         { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/bullets      { text }              → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/text/rewrite      { text, style }       → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (unchanged for Phase 3)

Bootstrap-project is a complex multi-step async Python workflow. Not a Phase 3 concern. Leave the existing endpoints.

```
POST   /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project
GET    /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/text/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes are gone)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- All instruction strings in `ai.service.ts` (the brainstorm prompt array, the style instruction map, etc.)
- The `generate()` method
- The `base = '/api/ai/text'` string

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end
5. Delete old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` routes
6. Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests
7. Delete dead TypeScript

aiTitle: Design thin-API phase 3 with flat text routes

content.text:
# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: thin-api-phase3

## Architecture Overview

Phase 3 finishes a migration that has been half-done since Phase 2: prompts move from frontend TypeScript and backend Python prompt-builder modules into SKILL.md files, and the HTTP surface collapses into eight flat, action-named routes. The mental model is a **facade**: `/api/text/<action>` is the public verb, the route handler is a ten-line glue layer, the skill is the brain. Each layer knows only what it needs — the route knows the action name and the input shape, the skill knows the prompt and the output shape, the frontend knows neither.

The key insight is that the eight current "text operations" are not eight different features — they are eight names for the same underlying call: send text, ask Claude to transform it, return text. Phase 2's mistake was treating that sameness as a reason to share a single `/rewrite` endpoint with instruction-string parameters. Phase 3 inverts that: the sameness lives in the *handler shape* (validate → call skill → return), while the *URL surface* fans out into eight verbs. This gives the frontend a typed, discoverable API and gives the backend independent prompt deployability per action.

The components fit as a one-way pipe. Angular's `AiService` exposes typed methods. Each method posts to a named route. Each route delegates to a named skill via the chain adapter. Each skill loads its SKILL.md and calls Claude. Nothing flows back upstream — no instruction string ever crosses a layer boundary. The only thing the frontend learns from the backend is `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Design Principles

| Principle | Application |
|-----------|-------------|
| **P1 Adapter Boundary** | All eight skill invocations go through `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py`; routes never touch a provider directly. The skill name is a parameter to the adapter, not a routing decision. |
| **P2 Thin HTTP Layer** | Each `/api/text/<action>` handler is roughly ten lines: auth → validate body → call skill → time response → return JSON. No conditional logic on action name inside any handler. |
| **P3 Async 202 + Polling** | Explicitly **not applied** here — these eight actions are sub-30s synchronous Claude calls. The async pattern stays reserved for `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide`, which Phase 3 leaves untouched. |
| **P4 No Speculative Abstractions** | Eight handlers, eight near-identical files. We do not build a generic dispatcher, a route factory, or an action registry. The handlers are short enough that copy is cheaper than abstraction. |
| **P5 OpenAPI-First** | The eight new routes are added to `openapi.yaml` first; DTOs and the contract for `style` enum are generated from it. The TypeScript `TextResponse` type and Python request validators trace back to the same source. |
| **P6 OpenClaw Plugin Principles** | SKILL.md is the single source of truth for prompt content. The six new skills (`expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`) follow the existing `brainstorm` and `rewrite` SKILL.md shape — no graduation to full plugin packages. |
| **P7 File Size** | `api/modules/ai/routes/text_actions.py` (the new blueprint) stays under 200 lines for all eight handlers combined. Each handler ~10 lines + shared validation helper keeps the math comfortable. |

## Component Design

### `/api/text/*` Blueprint (Backend Facade)

**Purpose**: Expose eight named verbs as the public contract for synchronous text transformations. Replace the single overloaded `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint that today disambiguates actions via instruction-string payloads.

The blueprint lives alongside the existing `text.py` route module but in a new file (`text_actions.py`) so the legacy file can be deleted in the same commit as the cutover. Each handler does four things in this order: enforce auth, parse and validate the request body, invoke the skill through the chain adapter, return the response with measured latency. The handlers share one private helper for the validate-and-call shape, but the helper is a function not a class — there is no inheritance and no per-action subclass.

The `style` enum on `/rewrite` is the only divergence from the uniform `{ text }` shape. Validation happens at the route boundary, not inside the skill — a 400 response for an unknown style value is a route concern, not a Claude concern. The five accepted values (`Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy`) are enumerated in `openapi.yaml` and mirrored in a Python literal/enum.

### Skill Layer (SKILL.md Authoring)

**Purpose**: Hold the actual instructions Claude receives. The skill is the only artifact that knows what "compress" means as a Claude instruction.

Two skills already exist (`brainstorm`, `rewrite`); six need authoring (`expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets`). Each follows the established SKILL.md shape from `plugin/skills/`. The author's goal for each new skill is small and constrained: a single-purpose transformation with no branching behavior. The brainstorm skill is allowed to be more complex because it handles the `question?` and `context?` optional fields — the followup-brainstorm caller routes through the same skill via additional body fields rather than spawning a separate `/brainstorm-followup` endpoint.

That decision matters. The braindump floated both options. The architectural choice is **single endpoint with optional fields** for brainstorm, because:
- It keeps the route count at exactly the eight named in the epic
- The skill is the right place for "do I have a follow-up question or not" branching — it's a prompt-shape concern, not a routing concern
- A new endpoint per minor variant would re-create the proliferation problem that motivated Phase 2

### Chain Adapter (Unchanged Boundary)

**Purpose**: Single seam between Flask and any AI provider. Phase 3 does not modify the adapter — it consumes the existing `generate()` / `rewrite()` interface.

What Phase 3 *does* change is how skills are addressed. The adapter is invoked with a skill name; the chain provider (claude-cli with `CHAIN_AGENT=chain-agent`) routes to the matching SKILL.md. This pattern already works for the existing two skills; the six new skills slot in identically.

### `AiService` (Frontend Thin Client)

**Purpose**: Typed Angular service exposing one method per action. Replaces the current `ai.service.ts` which embeds instruction strings and uses one HTTP method overloaded with prompt parameters.

After cutover, `AiService` has nine public methods (eight actions + a private `post` helper), no instruction strings, and no awareness of skills. Each method is approximately three lines. The base path becomes `/api/text` — the string `/api/ai/text` survives only in the two callers (bootstrap, epic-guide) that Phase 4 will address.

The `followupBrainstorm` flow in `app.component.ts` cuts over by calling `aiService.brainstorm(text, { question, context })` (or equivalent typed signature) — the component stops assembling instruction prose. The architecture decision (single brainstorm route, optional fields) drives this directly.

### Deletion Set

**Purpose**: A capability is also defined by what it removes. The cutover is incomplete until the old surface is gone.

The deletion set is treated as a first-class component because leaving it for "later" is the failure mode that produces dead code accumulation. Concretely: legacy routes (`/rewrite`, `/generate`, `/iterate`, `/lint-braindump`, `/review` under `/api/ai/text`), the `text_prompts.py` module and its tests, all instruction-string constants and the `generate()` method in `ai.service.ts`. The deletion happens in the same task as the cutover so the repo never enters a state where both surfaces work simultaneously.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Frontend | Angular 17 standalone + signals (existing) | No change. The work is removing code, not adding framework surface. |
| Frontend HTTP | `HttpClient` + `firstValueFrom` (existing pattern) | Matches the existing service shape; promises read cleaner at call sites than observables for one-shot AI calls. |
| Backend HTTP | Flask Blueprint (existing pattern) | New blueprint registered alongside `text.py`; same auth decorator, same JSON conventions. |
| AI Boundary | `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py` (existing) | P1 — only AI seam in the codebase. Adapter unchanged in Phase 3. |
| Prompt Storage | SKILL.md files in `plugin/skills/<action>/` | P6 — references are the source of truth; SKILL.md is the prompt artifact, deployable independently of code. |
| Contract | `openapi.yaml` (existing) | P5 — eight new routes plus `style` enum added there before any handler is written. |
| Validation | Route-level enum check for `style`; presence check for `text` | Validation at the boundary; the skill assumes a clean payload. |

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Eight flat routes instead of one parameterised route | Each action becomes a typed, named verb on both sides of the wire. Frontend gets discoverable methods; backend gets independently deployable prompts. The previous Phase 2 shape (single `/rewrite` with instruction strings) is exactly the antipattern this epic exists to fix. | More route entries, more SKILL.md files. Accepted because each route is ten lines and each skill is its own deployable artifact — the duplication is shape-only, not logic. |
| Single `/brainstorm` route handles followup via optional fields | Followup is a prompt-shape concern, not a routing concern. Adding `/brainstorm-followup` would re-introduce the proliferation we are removing. The skill branches internally on `question?` presence. | The brainstorm skill becomes the most complex of the eight. Acceptable because the complexity is genuinely there — it's not abstraction for its own sake, it's the one action that has two real shapes. |
| `style` enum validated at the route boundary, not in the skill | A bad enum value is a contract violation, not a generation failure. Returning 400 from the route is faster, cheaper, and clearer than letting the skill produce a degraded response. | A second source of truth for the enum (Python literal + OpenAPI schema). Mitigated by generating from `openapi.yaml`. |
| Delete `/api/ai/text/generate` with no successor | The generic `generate(prompt, tone)` endpoint had no clear business action and no current frontend caller. Re-deriving it later from one of the eight named actions is cheaper than maintaining it speculatively. | Any code path silently depending on it breaks. Audit during cutover; the epic confirms only the listed callers exist. |
| Bootstrap and epic-guide stay on `/api/ai/text/*` | They are async multi-step chains and need the 202+polling pattern. Migrating them is a different architectural problem (job state, status endpoint, error surface) that belongs in Phase 4. | The base path `/api/text` does not yet mean "all text endpoints" — it means "all *synchronous* text endpoints". Documented; the inconsistency is bounded and time-limited. |
| New blueprint file (`text_actions.py`) instead of editing `text.py` | The legacy file is being deleted. Editing it during the migration creates a confusing diff and a temporary file that must contain both old and new shapes. A new file lets the cutover commit add the new file and delete the old one cleanly. | One extra file in the tree during the transition window. Worth it for the clean diff. |
| No abstraction over the eight handlers | P4. Eight ten-line handlers that each call a skill by name produce a file under 200 lines with zero indirection. A generic dispatcher would save lines but obscure the action-to-skill mapping that is the whole point of Phase 3. | If a ninth action arrives, it costs a file, a route, a SKILL.md, and a TypeScript method — by design. That cost is the feature, not the bug. |
| Latency measurement happens at the route, not the adapter | `latencyMs` measures the user-visible round-trip the route layer is responsible for. Putting it in the adapter would either leak adapter timing semantics into the response or require duplicate timers. | Routes carry one extra concern. Acceptable — it's a `time.perf_counter()` pair, not architecture. |

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving design
- [Epic](./epic.md) – Scope and tasks
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking
